map_info.name: Facade_Venetian_Gothic
map_info.description: The hybridized expression of facade assembly. Two grammars compounding: Gothic vocabulary (pointed arches, quatrefoils, lacy tracery) embedded inside Italian-Renaissance bay rhythm and proportions. Ca' d'Oro / Palazzo Ducale as canonical reference. The principle still legible, but the column-order axis is replaced by a different ornamental vocabulary; the rhythm axis is Italian; the result is two languages speaking the same composition.

learning_objectives: Recognise the principle accommodating a foreign vocabulary at the column-order axis
Read two grammars compounding without either dissolving
Identify what the Italian rhythm structure does for the Gothic ornament

map_info.title: The Principle Hybridized

documentation.summary: Facade_Venetian_Gothic — the principle hybridized. Ca' d'Oro-style facade: Gothic pointed arches and quatrefoil tracery composed in Italian bay rhythm.
documentation.layout: 10x6 walkable space, same proportion as Classical to make the comparison direct. Spawn at back-centre. Teleporter on side.
documentation.objective: Show what happens when the column-order axis of the principle is *replaced* (not omitted) by an entirely different ornamental vocabulary while the rhythm and hierarchy axes stay Italian.
key_elements: Facade with pointed-arch arcade and quatrefoil tracery on front wall (artifacts queued)
